touches.text: VERBS: activate, charter, deposit, drain, feedback, question, sealed (plus get and show). Moving a ticket across its workflow is the ticket's own act; CodeMother's gates only answer it (3.3.4). Each chart stage (orient through validate) and the verdict is a gate machine that answers queueme <fileref>; the ticket class queues itself to each in turn (3.3.4.3), so there is no chart or verdict verb, and `cross` leaves with the harbor's `clear` (9.4.1.5). WHY: Akien, 2026-11-10, Q#81 ("should CodeMother answer a `chart` verb ... and a `verdict` verb?"): "yes, Q#81 closes on that", that being each stage and the verdict a gate with queueme, queued by the ticket class.

The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien. Akien, 2026-11-11, Q#85: "you and me. later there will be a specific agent for it, but that's so far off we're not even thinking about it now except 'after the outline is implemented'." So until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both of us read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.
